transcript.text: Some traders were like, I'm going to
watch here for the first candle to make
a new high. And I said, this is not a
bull flag. So, let's see. I'm going to
draw it out for you. All right. So,
we've got a big move up right here. This
is the part of the bull flag. And then
it pulls back. It dips down. Maybe one
red candle, maybe two, maybe three, and
then it continues higher. So, what are
important characteristics of a bull
flag? It should not retrace more than
50% of the initial move up. It should be
above the VWAP, which I have in my
dotted orange line. it should be above
the 9 EMA which I usually have in my
gray line here pulling back to the 90
EMA and the 20 moving average is usually
a little bit below and should be above
that as well. So these are the areas
that I'm kind of watching during a bull
flag. So if that's a bull flag, what you
see right here is certainly not a bull
flag. Yes, this rallied all the way up.
It came all the way back down. It's a
bounce off the VWAP, which is fine.
First fiveminute candle to make a new
high. All right. Well, it ends up
rallying back up. And I watched it and I
was like, I can't possibly because of
this candle.

metadata.title: Identifying a Bull Flag Pattern (Day Trading)
